item.content:encoded:
Anthropic makes Nasdaq debut after record USD 81 billion IPO, secures USD 1.5 trillion valuation Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. ANI | Updated: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 20:47 IST

Anthropic made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday. (Photo:Nasdaq). Image Credit: ANI

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Artificial intelligence (AI) company Anthropic, the developer of the Claude chatbot, made its Nasdaq debut on Thursday following a record USD 81.34 billion initial public offering (IPO), securing a valuation of approximately USD 1.5 trillion, according to Reuters. The landmark public offering comes amid growing investor interest in artificial intelligence companies, even as concerns persist over elevated valuations, the sustainability of AI-related investments and the potential emergence of a market bubble. According to the company's IPO details, Anthropic offered 980 million shares at USD 83 apiece, raising approximately USD 81.34 billion through the public offering. The company is listed on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the proposed ticker symbol 'ANT'. Reuters reported that the record IPO represents a major test of Wall Street's confidence in the AI boom, as investors weigh the technology's potential to transform the global economy against concerns over financial risks and its broader implications for humanity. The offering also comes alongside the latest earnings announcement from AI chipmaker Nvidia, with both developments serving as significant indicators of investor confidence in the rapidly expanding artificial intelligence industry. According to the financial details provided in the IPO filing, Anthropic reported revenue of USD 33.24 billion, while its net loss stood at approximately USD 104.04 billion. The company reported total assets of USD 154.32 billion and total liabilities of USD 146.68 billion, highlighting the scale of its financial operations. Anthropic, led by Chief Executive Officer Dario Amodei, had approximately 5,300 employees as of September 30, 2026. The IPO details also showed that the company had approximately 7.43 billion shares outstanding, while the offering included around 23.65 million shareholder shares. The record listing marks a significant milestone for the artificial intelligence industry, with Anthropic's market valuation placing it among the world's most highly valued technology companies. (ANI)

item.content:encoded:
South Korea's Lee says hopes reopening talks with North Korea could lead to lasting peace South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:55 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:55 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

South Korean President Lee Jae Myung said on Thursday he hoped a reopening of dialogue with North Korea would lead to discussions on ending the Korean War and establishing a lasting peace, as he addressed Asia-Pacific leaders in China. Speaking at a session of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, Lee said peace and stability on the Korean Peninsula were essential to shared regional prosperity and urged members to take an active interest and cooperate, according to the Korean presidential office. His statement came ahead of a trilateral summit between the leaders of Russia, China and the United States at APEC, with some analysts saying North Korea's nuclear weapons and sanctions on Pyongyang could be among the issues discussed. South Korea's National Security Adviser Wi Sung-lac told a briefing on Wednesday that Chinese President Xi Jinping told Lee at talks on the sidelines of the summit that Beijing would play a constructive role to realise peace on the Korean Peninsula. Lee also held a meeting with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney on Thursday at the summit, where they agreed to cooperate on building stable and mutually beneficial energy supply chains, according to Lee's office.

item.content:encoded:
Taiwan reports two Russian military aircraft nearby, second time this week Taiwan's defence ministry said that two Russian military Tu-95 aircraft flew to the island's east on Thursday after approaching from the south, the second time this week it has reported seeing such activity. Reuters | Updated: 19-11-2026 12:46 IST | Created: 19-11-2026 12:46 IST

SHARE

Key Takeaways AI Summary

Analyzing article...

Taiwan's defence ministry said that two Russian military Tu-95 aircraft flew to the island's east on Thursday after approaching from the south, the second time this week it has reported seeing such activity. The flights have come as Russian President Vladimir Putin is in China's Shenzhen for the APEC summit, where he will also hold a trilateral meeting with Chinese President Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump. The ministry said the two Tu-95s, known by NATO as "Bears", entered Taiwan's Air Defence Identification Zone, then exited airspace around Taiwan to the island's northeast, off the port city of Keelung. The ministry published a picture of one of the aircraft it said was taken from a Taiwanese F-16 fighter. Taiwan's armed forces used joint intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance means to monitor the full course of the activity and "responded appropriately", the ministry said in a short statement. Taiwan said on Tuesday two Russian military aircraft had flown in a southerly direction down its east coast. Japan also reported the same activity that day and published a map showing the aircraft flying down Taiwan's east coast. An ageing Cold War-era design, some Tu-95 can carry nuclear weapons but others of that type are used for long-range surveillance and reconnaissance. Russia's defence ministry has not responded to requests for comment. Earlier on Thursday, Taiwan's envoy to the APEC summit Stan Shih, the founder of computer maker Acer, briefly shook hands with Putin at the start of the summit. Major semiconductor producer Taiwan has joined Western countries in placing wide economic sanctions on Russia since it invaded Ukraine in 2022. China's military operates around Taiwan on a daily basis. China views Taiwan as its own territory, a position Russia has repeatedly backed. Taiwan's government rejects Beijing's sovereignty claims, saying only the island's people can decide their future.
